program: SNAP — no distinctive local nickname; CDHS calls it "Food Assistance" (see PROVENANCE.md)
agency: Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS), Division of Food and Energy Assistance
admin_note: Colorado is STATE-SUPERVISED, COUNTY-ADMINISTERED: CDHS's own description states Colorado "operates as a state supervised, county administered human services system," and each of Colorado's 64 counties' human services department is directly responsible for determining eligibility and authorizing SNAP benefits (SNAP Dispute Resolution Conferences happen at the county level; only Fair Hearings escalate to a state SNAP Hearings Unit). This matches this roster's Virginia/North Carolina independently-governed-county archetype, not Georgia/Indiana/Tennessee/Missouri/Maryland's state-agency-with-local-offices archetype. Confirm current operative practice (processing times, local outreach materials, exact office procedures) with the applicant's own county human services department, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD.
system: Colorado's eligibility technicians use the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS); applicants apply online through the Colorado PEAK portal, by the MyCOBenefits mobile app, in person, by mail, or by fax at a county human services office. Colorado Works is a SEPARATE, distinctly-named program (Colorado's TANF cash-assistance program) — not another name for SNAP.

Also fetched directly: CDHS's current SNAP page (cdhs.colorado.gov/snap), CDHS's current ABAWD FAQ page (cdhs.colorado.gov/snap/abawd), CDHS's current SNAP Healthy Choice Waiver status page (cdhs.colorado.gov/snap-healthy-choice-waiver), Colorado's own statute text via FindLaw's mirror of C.R.S. § 26-2-305, SB25-169 (Restaurant Meals Program) bill status via leg.colorado.gov, and abawdmap.us's Colorado-specific waiver-status entry. WebFetch (small-model summarization) was used for several HTML pages and returned two apparent date/detail errors this pack did NOT rely on without independent verification — see PROVENANCE.md Finding 0.
verification.gates: Colorado's own primary sources revealed the most extensive, most CLEARLY EXPLAINED staleness pattern this roster has documented: Colorado folds its entire operational SNAP policy directly into 10 CCR 2506-1, a FORMALLY PROMULGATED administrative regulation subject to Colorado's quarterly rulemaking cycle — unlike every other state in this roster, which maintains a separate, faster-to-revise narrative "manual" alongside its statute. This pack found NO separate Colorado manual; the CCR IS the manual. The likely consequence: as of this pack's fetch date, EVERY dollar figure in 10 CCR 2506-1 (maximum/minimum monthly allotments, the Standard Deduction, the Excess Shelter Deduction cap, the Homeless Shelter Deduction, and all four Standard Utility Allowances) is still labeled "Effective October 1, 2024" — the FFY2025 COLA cycle, one full federal fiscal year behind the current FFY2026 cycle (effective October 1, 2025) that this roster's other packs (MD, MO) independently confirmed via their own states' faster-moving transmittals. Only the 200% FPL income-limit table and the $3,000/$4,500 resource limits happen to be numerically identical between FFY2025 and FFY2026 nationally, so those two figures are confirmed CURRENT despite the CCR's own stale label. Separately and more strikingly, 10 CCR 2506-1-4.311 (ABAWD Work Requirements), despite its own header reading "[Effective 1/4/2025]," still defines an ABAWD as aged 18 through 54 and lists now-federally-REMOVED exemptions (homelessness, veteran status, aged-out-of-foster-care-by-24) — a genuine, disclosed internal contradiction against CDHS's own current, dated, OBBBA-updated ABAWD FAQ page and February 2026 training desk aid, both of which state the current federal 18-64 range. CDHS's own main /snap page compounds this: it states the ABAWD age range as "18 and 56" in one paragraph and "18 to 64" in another, on the SAME page, alongside a leftover stale 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act notice — a genuine, disclosed, THREE-WAY internal contradiction on a single Colorado government page. This pack treats CDHS's dedicated ABAWD FAQ page and February 2026 desk aid as authoritative for the ABAWD age range (18-64) because they are the most specific, most recently dated, and most directly OBBBA-responsive sources found. Separately, Colorado's own drug-felony rule is narrower than this pack expected from secondary "modified ban" characterizations — see PROVENANCE.md Finding 2 — and Colorado's Restaurant Meals Program and Healthy Choice Waiver are both live, actively-changing situations disclosed in freshness.json rather than stated as settled fact.
